by Hare Krishna Golden Temple · Vaishno Devi Helicopter Yatra

Take Mother Vaishno Devi's darshan the gentle way. A short helicopter flight from Katra to Sanjichhat replaces the 13 km climb, so yatris of every age can reach the Holy Cave, stay overnight at Bhawan, and sit before Mata Rani for the Atka Aarti at the main temple, which we arrange once for the group (evening or morning, as allotted). The yatra begins with the ancient temples of Jammu and ends with Banganga and Darshani Deodi at Katra, all in the association of ISKCON Hare Krishna devotees.

Punya Kshetras is the pilgrimage service of Hare Krishna Golden Temple, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad. Every yatra is led by devotees, with kirtan, japa and the glories of each holy place narrated along the way, sattvic food, careful planning and special attention to elders.
His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Srila Prabhupada,

The holy places all over the earth are meant for purifying the polluted consciousness of the human being by an atmosphere surcharged with the presence of the Lord's unalloyed devotees. If anyone visits a holy place, he must search out the pure devotees residing in such holy places, take lessons from them, try to apply such instructions in practical life and thus gradually prepare oneself for moksha.
Aarti at the Holy Cave, arranged for you
More time before Mata Rani; three Pindis
Your yatra, 13–16 March 2027, falls in a lovely window: pleasant days in Jammu and cool nights at Bhawan. Carry a shawl for the night at Bhawan.

Arrive at Jammu, the City of Temples, by 2 pm. After check-in and a late lunch at the hotel, take darshan at Sri Raghunath Temple and Ranbireshwar Temple, then browse Raghunath Bazaar for dry fruits and local crafts before returning to the hotel for kirtan and dinner.

Raghunath Temple, begun by Maharaja Gulab Singh in 1835 and completed by Maharaja Ranbir Singh in 1860, is dedicated to Lord Rama and houses a large collection of saligrama shilas. Ranbireshwar Temple is known for its tall Shiva lingam and twelve crystal lingams.

Katra – Helicopter to Vaishno Devi Bhawan

Drive to Katra at the foot of the Trikuta mountain, collect your RFID Yatra card and board the helicopter to Sanjichhat. A 2.5 km battery-car ride brings you to Bhawan. After rest and kirtan, enter the Holy Cave for darshan of the three Pindis. Our group's Atka Aarti at the main temple is arranged once – this evening or the next morning, as allotted by the Shrine Board.
In the Holy Cave the Mother is worshipped in the form of three natural rock Pindis, representing Maha Kali, Maha Lakshmi and Maha Saraswati. The shrine sits at about 5,200 ft on the Trikuta mountain.

Rise early for japa and darshan at Bhawan (or the Morning Atka Aarti, if that is our allotted slot), then take the ropeway to Bhairon Baba Temple. Walk down to Sanjichhat for the return flight to Katra. After lunch, take darshan at sacred Banganga and visit Darshani Deodi, the traditional gateway of the yatra, and Katra's market, then drive back to Jammu for the night at the same hotel as Day 1.
Tradition holds that the yatra is complete only after darshan at Bhairon Baba Temple. At Banganga, the Mother is believed to have shot an arrow into the earth to bring forth water.
